warnings: SECOND-FLOOR PLAN. The upper storey covers only the LEFT part of the building (grids 1-3, rows A-D); everything east of grid 3 is single storey, so roof appears on this plan rather than floor.

*** THIS SHEET SETTLES THE ROOF-COVERING QUESTION LEFT OPEN BY A-02. *** A-02 named fibre-cement double-corrugated tile OR profiled metal sheet without choosing. Here BOTH are used, on different parts: 'หลังคากระเบื้องลอนคู่' over the right wing and 'หลังคา METAL SHEET' over the car port and front terrace. It is not an either/or after all.

*** AND IT GIVES THE ROOF PITCH -- SLOPE 25° -- WHICH NO STRUCTURAL SHEET DOES. *** Three SLOPE 25° arrows are printed on the tiled wing, one per plane. The metal-sheet roof carries SLOPE arrows but NO angle, so its pitch is still unknown; flagged slope_not_printed.
Both roof areas are tagged 'โครงสร้างดูแบบวิศวกรรม' -- the architect defers the framing to the structural set. They correspond to S-05 (the hipped wing) and the S-04 terrace steel respectively.

The upper bathroom carries THREE levels: the room tag says +3.35 and two spot levels inside read +3.33 and +3.35, so the wet floor falls 0.02 m to the drain. The ground-floor bathroom used the same 0.02 m device against the +0.40 house floor.
FLOOR-TO-FLOOR IS 3.00 M: ground rooms at +0.40, upper rooms at +3.40.
RAILING TYPE DIFFERS BY FLOOR: the upper balcony calls railing 1 (A-20) while the ground-floor plan called railing 2 (A-21). Two different details, not one repeated.
The bathrooms stack -- the ช่องท่อ duct is in the same position on both floors, and WC1 (A-24) below sits under WC2 (A-27) here.
Opening marks carry the same door/window ambiguity as the ground-floor plan and are recorded by observed symbol shape only.
